matt (encops): Heads-up — our nightly backup scan flagged a handful of staging snapshots for tenant-228 that appear to be missing SSE metadata (no x-amz-server-side-encryption / x-amz-meta-encrypted). sizes/hashes look fine but metadata empty. noticed after yesterday's RBAC change to the uploader role.

olivia (sec-oncall): Ugh. Which bucket and keys? Can you paste a `head-object` output for one of the problematic files? Also tag SRE and backup-service.

matt (encops): Sure — example command and output:
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-staging-backups --key snapshots/tenant-228/2026-03-19T02:10:33Z.tar.gz
{
  "ContentLength": 10485760,
  "ContentType": "application/gzip",
  "ETag": "\"abcd1234efgh5678\"",
  "Metadata": {}
}
```
Note: metadata block is empty (we expect `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` and `x-amz-meta-encrypted: true`).

sam (sre): Did the backup job log a PutObject with SSE headers? Check CloudTrail/CloudAudit for PutObject events around 02:10 UTC and the principal used.

jess (backup-service): I can pull the job logs. Our service writes SSE-KMS headers as part of upload using the `backup-uploader` service account. Yesterday we rotated a role ARN for that account — possible IAM permission regression. Will grep the upload logs.

matt (encops): I already checked CloudTrail: several PutObject events exist but their `requestParameters.headers` looks like the SSE headers were omitted. Example CloudTrail snippet: `PutObject requestParameters: { key: "snapshots/tenant-228/...tar.gz", headers: {} }`.

olivia (sec-oncall): That suggests the uploader process ran but couldn't attach SSE. Could be missing kms:Encrypt or kms:GenerateDataKey on the CMK due to grant/role change. @kms-bot can you show recent grant audit for CMK `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01`?

kms-bot: Recent activity for CMK abcd-ef01:
- 2026-03-18T23:05Z: Grant created for `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader` (uuid: g-7785)
- 2026-03-19T01:42Z: Grant revoked (reason: role-rename) — matches timeline
- No regrant recorded.

jess (backup-service): OK this matches. Role rename triggered a revoke and we never re-created the grant. That would cause uploads to fall back to plaintext (or not set headers). I will pause new uploads to staging now.

sam (sre): Pause confirmed. I put a temporary deny rule on the `backup-uploader` role for PutObject to the backups bucket to prevent further clear uploads. :warning:

olivia (sec-oncall): Action items so far:
- jess: pause uploads and open a remediation runbook PR to re-create KMS grant + rotate affected snapshots OR re-encrypt in-place.
- matt: run a scan to enumerate all objects in `redwood-staging-backups` with empty SSE metadata and output list to /tmp/unencrypted-snapshots-3250001234.csv
- sam: hold the deny rule until we've confirmed remediation plan.
- I'll open an incident INC-2026-052 and notify Compliance for staging exposure (low-scope but need audit).

matt (encops): Scan results (first pass): 6 objects for tenant-228, 2 for tenant-199 (staging-only). I'll attach list to the incident.

jess (backup-service): Plan for remediation:
1) Recreate the KMS grant for `backup-uploader` against CMK abcd-ef01 (with kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey) — controlled by security.
2) Re-run upload job for affected snapshots to rewrite them with SSE-KMS (fastest) OR
3) If re-upload not possible, run a server-side re-encrypt pipeline: download -> reupload with correct headers (can be parallelized).
4) Add enforcement to backup pipeline: fail if `head-object` after upload doesn't show SSE headers.

olivia (sec-oncall): Approve the grant recreation. jess, please request the grant via standard KMS grant request ticket (include principal ARN + TTL for the grant). After grant is created, we can either re-run uploads or re-encrypt. Prefer re-upload for fidelity.

sam (sre): We should also add a Canary check in prod/staging that verifies `x-amz-server-side-encryption` is present within 60s of upload, and alert to #eng-sre / #eng-security. I'll open a quick PR for that.

matt (encops): Quick remediation note: for any affected snapshot that has already been downloaded by any downstream processes, treat as potential exposure — list of tenants and TTL of staging copies attached to INC-2026-052. Compliance notified.

jess (backup-service): I'll open the re-upload job and link the run in the incident when started. Also adding a postmortem draft explaining the grant ripple from role rename.

olivia (sec-oncall): Good. Assigning owners: jess -> remediation, sam -> guardrails/canary, matt -> enumeration + incident notes, olivia -> KMS grant approval + compliance comms. Keep updates in the incident thread. :thumbsup:

matt (encops): Update: created CSV /tmp/unencrypted-snapshots-3250001234.csv and uploaded to the incident. Starting re-upload attempts now.

jess (backup-service): Re-upload started for tenant-228 snapshots. First file re-upload succeeded and shows `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` on `head-object`. Will proceed.

sam (sre): Canary PR open: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/420 — alerting to #eng-sre and #eng-security on failures.

olivia (sec-oncall): Closing interim loop: stop the deny once we confirm all affected objects rewritten or re-encrypted. Keep INC-2026-052 open until postmortem. Thanks team. :eyes:

matt (encops): noted. I'll add a check to the backup-service integration tests to simulate grant revocation and ensure uploads fail loudly next time.

jess (backup-service): PRs for enforcement + reupload run linked in incident. Will post final status when all 8 objects are verified.

kms-bot: Grant recreation completed at 2026-03-19T03:12Z (uuid: g-7790) for principal `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader`.
